18	The Defendants contend that the Complaint should be dismissed in its entirety for failure to comply with the 2004 Agreement’s dispute resolution and mediation clause. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. 18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:

18	The more significant problem with Love-joy’s argument that it had an “unfettered” right to redefine the House Accounts is that this interpretation would nullify portions of the Agreement’s termination provision. PL’s Opp. Br. at 17. Under the termination provision, the Agreement became effective January 1, 2004, and:
19	shall continue in force for a one (1) year period, and shall be automatically renewed for additional one (1) year periods thereafter unless terminated by written notice from either party to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the initial or any subsequent one (1) year term.

Id. Finally, the Agreement expressly contemplates that the parties could terminate the Agreement at any time by “mutual written agreement.” Id.
21	The termination provision, on its face, provides a comprehensive account of the ways in which the Agreement may be terminated. There is no indication in the Agreement that the parties contemplated that the House Accounts provision would constitute an additional means for terminating all of Lovejoy’s obligations under the Agreement. Under Lovejoy’s construction of the House Accounts provision, however, Lovejoy could, at any time and without Kamco’s consent, redefine every single account in Kamco’s territory as a House Account. This interpretation would allow Lovejoy to escape from all of its obligations under the Agreement and all of the restrictions in the termination provision.
22	This reading is inconsistent with Pennsylvania law, which, as noted above, forbids courts from “interpreting] one provision of a contract in a manner which results in another portion being annulled,” LJL Transp., 962 A.2d at 648 (citation omitted), and requires that “[t]he whole instrument ... be taken together in arriving at contractual intent,” Duquesne Univ., 777 A.2d at 429 (citation omitted). In other words, the “mutual” termination provision would never apply to Lovejoy.

This purpose would obviously be frustrated if one party maintained a unilateral right to opt out of all of its obligations under the contract at any time — which is precisely how Lovejoy construes the House Accounts provision.
24	This court’s conclusion that Lovejoy’s reading of the House Accounts provision is inconsistent with the parties’ intent is reinforced by the fact that the Agreement contains a non-compete provision. The noncompetition provision states that Kamco could not, without Lovejoy’s permission, sell any product which is directly competitive with any Lovejoy product that Kamco was supposed to sell on Lovejoy’s behalf. Id. ¶ 2. If, as Lovejoy suggests, the House Accounts provision granted Lovejoy the “unfettered” right to redefine all or substantially all accounts as House Accounts, then Lovejoy would have the unilateral power to deprive Kamco of all of the benefits it was to receive under the contract while simultaneously barring Kamco from selling any product made by a Lovejoy competitor. Good faith duties are implied “where it is clear that an obligation is within the contemplation of the parties at the time of contracting or is necessary to carry out their intentions.” Slater v. Pearle Vision Center, Inc., 376 Pa.Super. 580, 546 A.2d 676, 679 (1988); see also Duquesne Light, 66 F.3d at 617 (noting that “courts generally utilize the good faith duty as an interpretive tool to determine the parties’ justifiable expectations”). Reading the House Accounts provision in this manner allows the termination provision to have its intended effect: If one of the parties wishes to put an end to its obligations to the other party, it must follow one of the enumerated ways of terminating the Agreement.

“Master Servicer’) and as securities administrator (in such capacity, the “Securities
Administrator”), and DEUTSCHE BANK NATIONAL TRUST COMPANY, a national banking
association, as trustee (the “Trustee”).

PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

The Depositor is the owner of the Trust Fund that is hereby conveyed to the Trustee in
return for the Certificates.

REMIC I

As provided herein, the Securities Administrator on behalf of the Trustee shall elect to
treat the segregated pool of assets consisting of the Mortgage Loans and certain other related
assets subject to this Agreement (other than the Reserve Fund, the Yield Maintenance
Agreement, the Yield Maintenance Collateral Account and any Prepayment Charge Waiver
Amounts and, for the avoidance of doubt, the Supplemental Interest Trust, the Swap Agreement,
the Swap Account, the Swap Collateral Account and any rights or obligations in respect of the
Swap Administration Agreement) as a REMIC for federal income tax purposes, and such
segregated pool of assets will be designated as “REMIC I”. The Class R-1 Certificates will
represent the sole class of Residual Interests in REMIC I for purposes of the REMIC Provisions.
The following table irrevocably sets forth the designation, the Uncertificated REMIC I Pass-
Through Rate, the initial Uncertificated Principal Balance and, for purposes of satisfying
Treasury Regulation Section 1.860G-1(a)(4)(iii), the “latest possible maturity date” for each of
the REMIC I Regular Interests. None of the REMIC I Regular Interests will be certificated.

5734	Section 4.22 Reserve Fund; Payments to and from Swap Administrator; Supplemental
5735	Interest Trust; Yield Maintenance Agreement.
5736	
5737	(a) Pursuant to the Swap Administration Agreement, the Supplemental Interest Trust
5738	shall be established and maintained in the name of the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee, as a
5739	separate trust, the corpus of which shall be held by the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee, for
5740	the benefit of the Holders of the Class A, Class M, Class B and Class CE Certificates and the
5741	Swap Provider. The Supplemental Interest Trust shall hold the Swap Agreement, the Swap
5742	Administration Agreement, REMIC VI Regular Interest IO, the Swap Collateral Account and the
5743	Swap Account. The Swap Account shall be an Eligible Account, and funds on deposit therein
5744	shall be held separate and apart from, and shall not be commingled with, any other moneys,
5745	including, without limitation, other moneys of the Trustee held pursuant to this Agreement.
5746	Amounts in the Swap Account shall, at the direction of the Majority Class CE Certificateholder,
5747	be invested in Permitted Investments that mature no later than the Business Day prior to the next
5748	succeeding Distribution Date. All net income and gain from such investments shall be distributed
5749	to the Class CE Certificateholders, on a pro rata basis, not as a distribution in respect of any
5750	interest in any REMIC, on such Distribution Date. In the absence of written instructions to the
5751	Securities Administrator, amounts on deposit in the Swap Account shall remain uninvested. All

Section 4.22 Reserve Fund; Payments to and from Swap Administrator; Supplemental
Interest Trust; Yield Maintenance Agreement.

(a) Pursuant to the Swap Administration Agreement, the Supplemental Interest Trust
shall be established and maintained in the name of the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee, as a
separate trust, the corpus of which shall be held by the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee, for
the benefit of the Holders of the Class A, Class M, Class B and Class CE Certificates and the
Swap Provider. The Supplemental Interest Trust shall hold the Swap Agreement, the Swap
Administration Agreement, REMIC VI Regular Interest IO, the Swap Collateral Account and the
Swap Account. The Swap Account shall be an Eligible Account, and funds on deposit therein
shall be held separate and apart from, and shall not be commingled with, any other moneys,
including, without limitation, other moneys of the Trustee held pursuant to this Agreement.
Amounts in the Swap Account shall, at the direction of the Majority Class CE Certificateholder,
be invested in Permitted Investments that mature no later than the Business Day prior to the next
succeeding Distribution Date. All net income and gain from such investments shall be distributed
to the Class CE Certificateholders, on a pro rata basis, not as a distribution in respect of any
interest in any REMIC, on such Distribution Date. In the absence of written instructions to the
Securities Administrator, amounts on deposit in the Swap Account shall remain uninvested. All
amounts earned on amounts on deposit in the Swap Account shall be taxable to the Class CE
Certificateholders. Any losses on such investments shall be deposited in the Swap Account by
the Majority Class CE Certificateholder out of its own funds immediately as realized, on a pro
rata basis. In performing its duties hereunder and under the Swap Agreement and Swap
Administration Agreement, the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee shall be entitled to the same
rights, protections and indemnities as provided to the Securities Administrator hereunder. On
each Distribution Date, the Securities Administrator shall remit such amounts received from the
Swap Administrator to the Holders of the Class A, Class M and Class B Certificates in \ the
manner provided in clause (e) below.

Section 1.02 Allocation of Certain Interest Shortfalls.

For purposes of calculating the amount of Current Interest for the Class A, Class M,
Class B and Class CE Certificates for any Distribution Date, the aggregate amount of any
Prepayment Interest Shortfalls (to the extent not covered by payments by the related Servicer
pursuant to the related Servicing Agreement or the Master Servicer pursuant to Section 6.02) and
any Relief Act Interest Shortfalls incurred in respect of the Mortgage Loans for any Distribution
Date shall be allocated first, to the Class CE Interest based on, and to the extent of, one month’s
interest at the then applicable Pass-Through Rate on the Uncertificated Notional Amount of such
interest and, thereafter, among the Class A, Class M and Class B Certificates, in each case on a
pro rata basis, based on, and to the extent of, one month’s interest at the then applicable
respective Pass-Through Rates on the respective Certificate Principal Balances of each such
Certificate.

For purposes of calculating the amount of Uncertificated Accrued Interest for the REMIC
I Regular Interests for any Distribution Date, the aggregate amount of any Prepayment Interest
Shortfalls (to the extent not covered by the related Servicer pursuant to the related Servicing
Agreement or the Master Servicer pursuant to Section 6.02) and any Relief Act Interest
Shortfalls incurred in respect of the Mortgage Loans for any Distribution Date shall be allocated
first, to REMIC I Regular Interest I-Non-Swap and the REMIC I Regular Interests ending with
the designation “B”, pro rata, based on, and to the extent of, one month’s interest at the then
applicable respective Uncertificated REMIC I Pass-Through Rates on the respective

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c132","reasoning_cat1":"Names DTC, allows substitution by any registered clearing agency and imposes a UCC 'clearing corporation' status requirement; each element is definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Book-Entry Certificates and Certificateholder definitions naming Cede & Co.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c133","reasoning_cat1":"Refers to 'the Class of Book-Entry Certificates' in the singular although several classes are book-entry, a small mechanical slip.","reasoning_cat2":"The Book-Entry Certificates definition names multiple classes, so the singular reference is mildly inconsistent with it.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c134","reasoning_cat1":"'Other Person for whom ... a Depository effects book-entry transfers' is a general catch-all after a list of financial institutions, but the functional test that follows bounds it.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Book-Entry Certificates definition's use of 'Depository Participant'.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c135","reasoning_cat1":"Two different dates apply depending on which Servicer holds the loan, so 'the Determination Date' has no single value for a given Distribution Date.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.03 requires the Purchase Price and Substitution Adjustment Amount to be deposited 'on the Determination Date for the Distribution Date', which is indeterminate when a repurchase spans servicers.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c136","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated agreement and its form exhibit; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit J-1 and the Custodial Agreements definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c137","reasoning_cat1":"The definition runs into a free-standing operative sentence ('... shall be held in trust for the Certificateholders'), leaving it grammatically incomplete as a definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the account is created 'pursuant to Section 5.08', but the Agreement's Article V ends at Section 5.04 and the Distribution Account is established under Section 5.02, so the cross-reference does not resolve.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c138","reasoning_cat1":"A definite date convention with a business-day roll and a stated commencement month.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Business Day and Interest Accrual Period definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c139","reasoning_cat1":"A short definition by reference to a securities filing; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.18's reporting scheme.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c140","reasoning_cat1":"Definite by reference to the Mortgage Note.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Due Period and Scheduled Payment definitions.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c141","reasoning_cat1":"A precise period definition running from the second day of one month to the first day of the next.","reasoning_cat2":"Used throughout the principal distribution formulas; one of those (Class M-6) mismatches it, but the defect lies in that formula rather than here.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c142","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference to Section 4.18.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.18 exists and uses EDGAR.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c143","reasoning_cat1":"A three-branch definition whose clause (iii) — 'any other account acceptable to the Rating Agencies' — is a wide-open catch-all sitting against two specific rating-based tests, and the phrase 'such institution's rating above' is garbled.","reasoning_cat2":"The closing sentence expressly overrides Section 12.01 to permit amendment of the rating requirements without Certificateholder consent, which is a definition purporting to displace the Agreement's amendment provision.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c144","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line entity identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Seller definition, which names EMC and the Sponsor.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},

{"clause_id":"c147","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference to Section 9.01.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 9.01 is the Events of Default provision per the table of contents.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c148","reasoning_cat1":"A two-part sum of defined amounts; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Excess Spread and Overcollateralization Release Amount definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c149","reasoning_cat1":"Definite excess calculation, subject to a legal carve-out for amounts owed to the Mortgagor.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Liquidation Proceeds definition.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c150","reasoning_cat1":"Definite arithmetic with a parenthetical carve-out keyed to a subsection.","reasoning_cat2":"It excludes Interest Carry Forward Amounts 'paid pursuant to Section 6.04(a)(3)(A)', a subsection outside the supplied operative text, so the carve-out cannot be verified here.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c192","reasoning_cat1":"One line, definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the MERS, MIN and MOM Loan definitions and Section 2.01's MERS carve-outs.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c193","reasoning_cat1":"One line, definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01(ii) and Mortgage Loan Schedule item (x).","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c194","reasoning_cat1":"Definite by reference to the Mortgage Note.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Maximum Mortgage Rate and Periodic Rate Cap definitions.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c195","reasoning_cat1":"The definition defines a loan type by describing MERS's role rather than the loan, so grammatically it defines the wrong thing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.01(ii)-(iii) turns delivery obligations on whether a loan 'is a MOM Loan', so the mis-framed definition has operative bite.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c196","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference to Section 6.06.","reasoning_cat2":"Article VI is outside the supplied operative text but the table of contents matches.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"Entity identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Rating Agency definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c198","reasoning_cat1":"'Or other instrument creating a first lien' is a catch-all after two specific instruments, and it asserts a first lien even though the Mortgage Loan Schedule contemplates second lien loans.","reasoning_cat2":"Mortgage Loan Schedule items (g) and (s) expressly contemplate second lien Mortgage Loans, which cannot satisfy this first-lien-only definition of Mortgage.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c199","reasoning_cat1":"Defined by reference to the Section 2.01 list plus 'any additional documents delivered ... to be added'; the open second limb is soft but workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.01's closing paragraph and Sections 2.02(a)-(b) use Mortgage File consistently with this definition.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"The second sentence creates a deeming rule for loans never in fact transferred, which is an operative rule buried in a definition and turns on the elastic phrase 'intended by the parties hereto to be transferred'.","reasoning_cat2":"It cites 'the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v)', but Section 2.03(b) of this Agreement is a single survival sentence with no subclauses, so the cross-reference has no referent.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated agreement and its form exhibit; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.01 and Section 2.02(d) both build on this agreement, and Exhibit L matches the exhibit list.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c202","reasoning_cat1":"A short cross-reference definition; definite on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits alongside the separately defined 'Purchase Price', and the two similarly named terms govern different repurchase mechanisms (Section 11.01 versus Sections 2.02/4.21), inviting confusion.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c203","reasoning_cat1":"The enumeration is mechanically broken: two different items are lettered '(aa)', one label is garbled, 'the the Periodic Rate Cap' and 'whether the Mortgage Loan is has a balloon payment' are ungrammatical, and several items are '[reserved]'.","reasoning_cat2":"The list contains no field identifying the Originator, yet the Originator definition says the originator is 'set forth in the Mortgage Loan Schedule'; item (ee) gives only the related Seller.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c204","reasoning_cat1":"'Or other evidence of indebtedness' is a mild catch-all but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's delivery requirements and the lost-note alternative.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c205","reasoning_cat1":"One line, definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Net Mortgage Rate and Adjustable Rate Mortgage Loan definitions.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c206","reasoning_cat1":"Very short and broad ('the underlying property'), but unlikely to be disputed.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Mortgage and Appraised Value definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"One line, plural 'obligors' handled sensibly.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with usage throughout.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.02},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"A clean three-part subtraction.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Fee Rate, Master Servicing Fee Rate and LPMI Fee definitions.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"A long formula with a swap deduction converted to a rate and a separate tax definition; the placement of 'multiplied by 12' and the actual/360 adjustment sentence leave the order of operations arguable.","reasoning_cat2":"It gives one Net Rate Cap for the Certificates and a different one 'for federal income tax purposes' for the corresponding REMIC III Regular Interests, which the Preliminary Statement footnote also flags; reconciling the two requires care but they are expressly kept apart.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite, with an express exclusion of Swap Termination Payments.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22(c)'s ordering of Net Swap Payments before Swap Termination Payments.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"Turns wholly on 'the good faith judgment' of the advancing party as to ultimate recoverability, with an open 'or otherwise' source of recovery — a genuinely elastic standard.","reasoning_cat2":"The Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions deduct Nonrecoverable Advances, so the judgment call has direct cash-flow consequences, but no provision contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.14},

{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"A short three-term formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Principal Funds, Extra Principal Distribution Amount and Overcollateralization Release Amount definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (d) runs several repurchasers together without conjunctions and ends with the unexplained phrase 'or by another Servicer'; limb (f) mixes Due Period and prior-calendar-month measures.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (e) points to substitutions 'pursuant to Section 2.03(d)', but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b), and limb (d) omits EMC even though the Seller definition includes it.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, with an express inclusion of repurchases and a rule for partial prepayments.","reasoning_cat2":"It treats repurchases under Sections 2.02, 2.03, 4.21 and 11.01 as Principal Prepayments, which fits the Principal Funds definition's separate limb for repurchase proceeds only loosely.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list.","reasoning_cat2":"The Book-Entry Certificates definition says Class B-4 is book-entry while the Global/Individual Certificate definitions assume Private Certificates may be either; reconcilable but overlapping.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated document; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"The Prospectus Supplement is not attached as an exhibit, yet the Prepayment Assumption definition depends on it.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"Definite by reference to the Servicing Agreements.","reasoning_cat2":"Listed in the Account definition and referenced in Section 2.01's prepaid-loan proviso; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the ungrammatical 'plus and (iii)', and the reduction for Servicing Fee, Servicing Advances and Advances 'payable to the purchaser' is placed so that its reach over limbs (i) and (ii) is unclear.","reasoning_cat2":"It is defined only for repurchases 'pursuant to Section 2.02' and purchases under Section 4.21, yet Section 2.03 and the Mortgage Loans definition also require payment of 'the Purchase Price' for Seller and Originator repurchases, leaving those repurchases without a defined price.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.50},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, with a successor mechanism and a modifier-stripping rule.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Eligible Account and Permitted Investments rating tests.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"Four separate branches with different measurement conventions, and it repeatedly uses 'Monthly Payment', which the Agreement does not define (the defined term is Scheduled Payment).","reasoning_cat2":"The undefined 'Monthly Payment' also appears in the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition, and the Realized Loss branches must be reconciled with the Subsequent Recoveries and Applied Realized Loss Amount definitions.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"Two symmetrical rules keyed to book-entry status; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Book-Entry Certificates and Private Certificates definitions.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c250","reasoning_cat1":"'Leading banks selected by the Securities Administrator' is a discretionary and vague qualifier, though the three lettered conditions narrow it.","reasoning_cat2":"The independence condition excludes affiliates of 'the Depositor, the Seller or the Master Servicer' but not the Securities Administrator itself, which is the selector.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed fallback rate mechanic with rounding conventions and a quorum rule; precise.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the One-Month LIBOR and Reference Banks definitions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06}
]}

{"clause_id":"c282","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to form and execution, with an electronic-delivery deeming rule; the closing 'of the related Servicer, as applicable' is stray.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.02(c) and 2.03, which condition release of Mortgage Files on receipt of a Request for Release, and with Exhibit G.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c283","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line account definition; nothing ambiguous on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the Reserve Fund is created 'pursuant to Section 6.08', but Section 6.08 is the Class P Certificate Account and Section 4.22(b) is what actually establishes the Reserve Fund.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c284","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed dollar amount; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"It too cites Section 6.08 for the deposit, whereas Section 4.22(b) directs the Depositor to deposit the Reserve Fund Deposit into the Reserve Fund.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c285","reasoning_cat1":"Definite list with an explanatory parenthetical.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Class R and Class RX Certificate definitions and Sections 2.06(d)-(f).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c286","reasoning_cat1":"Incorporates the Code definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC recitals naming a sole residual class for each REMIC.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c287","reasoning_cat1":"After a specific list of offices it adds 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers or other officers of the Trustee specified by the Trustee' — an open catch-all that swallows the list.","reasoning_cat2":"Responsible Officer knowledge is the trigger for the Trustee's duties in Article X, which is outside the supplied text, so the practical fit cannot be fully checked here.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c288","reasoning_cat1":"Entity identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Rating Agency definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c289","reasoning_cat1":"Entity identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicer definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c290","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated agreement and exhibit; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"The exhibit list places the Saxon Assignment, Assumption and Recognition Agreement at Exhibit R-2, while this definition points to Exhibit R-3 (the Wells Fargo agreement).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c291","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated agreement and exhibit; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit Q-2 in the exhibit list and the Servicing Agreement definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c292","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Several provisions (Realized Loss, Mortgage Loan Schedule) instead use the undefined 'Monthly Payment', which sits awkwardly beside this definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c293","reasoning_cat1":"Statutory reference.","reasoning_cat2":"No conflict.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.02},
{"clause_id":"c294","reasoning_cat1":"Definite; expressly bundles three capacities.","reasoning_cat2":"The separate Paying Agent definition duplicates one of those capacities, a redundancy rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c295","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.18(b) exists.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c296","reasoning_cat1":"'Any of EMC and the Sponsor' is grammatically odd but the referents are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Several definitions (Interest Funds, Principal Funds) name only the Sponsor or the Originator as repurchasers and omit EMC, which is inconsistent with EMC's status as a Seller obliged to repurchase under Section 2.02(d).","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c297","reasoning_cat1":"A closed three-item list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Agreement and Assignment Agreement definitions.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c298","reasoning_cat1":"'All customary, reasonable and necessary out of pocket costs ... including, but not limited to' four enumerated categories is an open catch-all against specifics, and the final sentence uses 'Nonrecoverable Servicing Advances', a term the Agreement never defines.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement defines only 'Nonrecoverable Advance' (advances of principal and interest), so the closing sentence's limit has no defined content elsewhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c299","reasoning_cat1":"A closed three-item list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the three named servicing agreements and the Servicer definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c300","reasoning_cat1":"The alternative limb — criteria 'otherwise mutually agreed to ... in response to evolving interpretations of Regulation AB' — is open-ended in both content and trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"It permits a revised Exhibit N by agreement of EMC, the Master Servicer, the Trustee and the Servicer without the amendment procedure of Section 12.01 or the Depositor's participation.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c301","reasoning_cat1":"A clean per-loan fee formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Fee Rate and Net Mortgage Rate definitions; unlike the Master Servicing Fee it contains no float add-on.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c302","reasoning_cat1":"A single rate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Fee definition; the Mortgage Loan Schedule also carries a per-loan Servicing Fee Rate field, which could vary from this flat rate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c303","reasoning_cat1":"Turns on being 'involved in, or responsible for' servicing plus 'evidence reasonably acceptable to the Trustee ... of due authorization', which is circular and does not say what happens absent such evidence.","reasoning_cat2":"Servicing Officer certifications are required by the Request for Release definition and Section 2.01's prepaid-loan proviso, so the identification gap has operative consequences.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c304","reasoning_cat1":"Rests on a 'reasonable good-faith estimate' of an aggregate exposure with no stated methodology in the instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"It assigns the estimate to 'EMC or its affiliate', whereas the Maximum Probable Exposure definition it builds on assigns the calculation to the Depositor using EMC's internal process — the two do not line up.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c305","reasoning_cat1":"A straightforward ratio.","reasoning_cat2":"Inherits the indeterminacy of the Significance Estimate definition but is otherwise consistent with Item 1115 reporting in Section 4.18.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c306","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed dollar amount with an explanatory gloss; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.01 says the Special Deposit 'will be transferred by EMC', while this definition says it is 'deposited into the Trust by the Depositor' — a direct inconsistency about who makes the deposit.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c307","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line entity identification.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.02(d) gives the Sponsor a backstop repurchase obligation for Accredited-originated loans, which is consistent with this capacity definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c308","reasoning_cat1":"One line, definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Closing Date definition and the REMIC recitals.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c309","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (i) subtracts principal 'due ... during each Due Period' without saying which Due Periods are counted relative to the Distribution Date, and there is a special two-month rule for the first Distribution Date.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the input to almost every distribution formula and to the Overcollateralization definitions; the parallel loss-measurement mismatches in the Class M-4 and M-6 formulas trace back to this definition's Prepayment Period convention.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.20},

{"clause_id":"c311","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Class M, Class B, Class CE and Residual Certificate definitions.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04}

{"clause_id":"c312","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence is structurally mangled — 'amounts received ... or surplus amounts held ... to cover estimated expenses (including ... recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller) specifically related to a Mortgage Loan' — so it is unclear whether representation-and-warranty recoveries are Subsequent Recoveries or merely examples of estimated expenses.","reasoning_cat2":"That matters because Section 2.02(d) and Section 2.03 route breach-of-representation recoveries through the repurchase machinery and the Purchase Price, not through Subsequent Recoveries, and the Certificate Principal Balance definition adds Subsequent Recoveries back under a non-existent Section 5.04(b).","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.35},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c351","reasoning_cat1":"A single date; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Yield Maintenance Agreement definition and Section 4.22(b).","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c352","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line account definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It cites Section 5.04, which the table of contents titles 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex' rather than an account-creation provision; the Certificate Principal Balance definition also cites Section 5.04(b) for an unrelated purpose.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to parties and date.","reasoning_cat2":"The Yield Maintenance Agreement definition already sweeps in any credit support annex, and Section 5.04 bears the same heading, so this term is duplicative.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"Three long parallel allocation paragraphs; mechanical and internally consistent, if hard to read.","reasoning_cat2":"It dovetails with the Current Interest and Uncertificated Accrued Interest definitions, which both point back to this section; the reference to Section 6.02 coverage is outside the supplied text.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"The granting language is garbled in places ('all the right, title and interest of the Sellers in and to the assets in the Mortgage Loans'), and the delivery obligations shift unpredictably between 'the Depositor' and 'the Seller may deliver', with a one-year title-policy grace built into limb (v).","reasoning_cat2":"Its final paragraph says the Special Deposit 'will be transferred by EMC', while the Special Deposit definition says it is 'deposited into the Trust by the Depositor'; and the conveyance of 'the Trust Fund' must be squared with the Trust Fund definition, which omits the Bring Down Agreements that Section 2.02(d) requires the Trustee to enforce.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the ungrammatical 'will deliver to the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee an Initial Certification', and the review standard mixes a duty to 'ascertain' with permission to 'conclusively rely' on execution and genuineness.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to loans 'identified in Exhibit B to this Agreement, as supplemented', while the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition contemplates amendment for substitutions rather than supplementation; the interaction with Section 2.02(c)'s cure/repurchase remedy is also left implicit.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"A definite 180-day review with a stated notification duty; 'appear defective on its face' is a soft but conventional standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Custodian to notify only 'the Sellers', whereas Section 2.02(c) makes both the Sellers and the related Originators potential repurchasers of defective loans.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"The closing sentence makes cure/repurchase/substitution 'the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — a limitation that names two persons but conspicuously omits the Trustee and the Trust, an expressio unius problem on the face of the words.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.02(d) separately empowers the Trustee to enforce repurchase obligations 'on behalf of the Trust', and Section 2.03 provides a separate repurchase mechanic, so the reach of this sole-remedy sentence against those provisions is genuinely contestable.","prob_cat1":0.58,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"The duty extends to repurchase obligations 'and any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation' the Sponsor's Accredited backstop — a general catch-all followed by one specific, raising ejusdem generis and expressio unius questions about the backstop's scope.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be read against Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence and against the Trust Fund definition, which conveys 'the rights under the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement' but does not mention the Bring Down Agreements the Trustee is told to enforce.","prob_cat1":0.55,"prob_cat2":0.53},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"The notice paragraph turns on 'discovery' of a breach that 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders' and requires 'prompt written notice', all elastic terms; the deposit timing is keyed to the Determination Date, of which there are two.","reasoning_cat2":"The section is headed as containing only the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations, yet it houses the substitution and repurchase machinery that the Replacement Mortgage Loan definition, Section 2.05 and Section 4.02 all cross-refer to as if it contained loan-level representations.","prob_cat1":0.49,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence survival clause; on its own terms it is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the Section 2.03 representations survive 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', which makes sense only for loan-level representations, whereas Section 2.03 contains corporate representations of Wells Fargo; the Mortgage Loans definition also cites a non-existent 'Section 2.03(b)(v)' representation.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.46},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"The final paragraph reads 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach', omitting a conjunction, and the good-title representation is given without any stated remedy for its breach.","reasoning_cat2":"The Depositor's good-title representation sits against Section 2.01's conveyance and Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence, which addresses only document defects, leaving unclear what follows from a breach of this representation.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"Opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and turns on whether 'default is not reasonably foreseeable', a forward-looking judgment with no decision-maker specified.","reasoning_cat2":"It overrides the repurchase timing in Sections 2.02 and 2.03, which themselves set fixed Determination Date deposit dates, so the two timing regimes must be reconciled.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"Gives the Seller or Originator an option among cure, substitution and repurchase 'at such party's option', with a 90-day outside date attaching only to limb (iii).","reasoning_cat2":"It requires substitution to satisfy 'the conditions in Section 2.03', but Section 2.03's substitution paragraph bars any substitution after the second anniversary of the Closing Date, which would leave later-discovered non-qualified mortgages with only cure or repurchase.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"A short acknowledgment and declaration of trust; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and the Trustee definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC II recital and the Class R-2 Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC III recital and the Class R-3 Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC IV recital and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC V recital and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC VI recital, Section 4.22(a) and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"Limbs (d) and (e) are open-ended catch-alls ('necessary, suitable or convenient ... or are incidental thereto or connected therewith') sitting against three specific purposes, and the final sentence trails off with the dangling 'and this Section 2.07'.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (b) says the Trust issues 'the Certificates sold to the Depositor in exchange for the Mortgage Loans', while Section 2.01 and the Preliminary Statement describe the exchange as being for the whole Trust Fund.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"Grants 'full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable' and then imposes a series of specific monitoring duties, so the interaction of the open grant with the specific duties is contestable.","reasoning_cat2":"The open grant sits against the objective Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard in the same section and against Section 4.05's identically worded grant, which is expressly made subject to the REMIC Provisions.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Three specific prohibitions with defined exceptions; reasonably tight, though 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer' is an unqualified obedience duty.","reasoning_cat2":"It excepts substitutions 'pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or Section 2.03 of this Agreement', consistently with Section 2.03's substitution paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"Turns on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment' and on what it 'deems appropriate', and permits reliance on an Officer's Certificate without further inquiry.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out for Wells Fargo as Servicer aligns with Section 4.03(b)-(c), which route Wells Fargo terminations through the Trustee instead.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"The enforcement standard — such extent and time as the Master Servicer 'in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans' — is an elastic hypothetical-owner test, and the last sentence's 'Successor master Servicer' is inconsistently capitalised.","reasoning_cat2":"The final sentence conditions the Trustee's assumption of duties on the Trustee 'not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the mandatory termination duties earlier in the same subsection and with Section 8.07.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"Two long parallel reimbursement regimes, each with an 'including, without limitation' list; the trigger 'not fully and timely reimbursed' has no stated deadline.","reasoning_cat2":"Reimbursement comes from the Distribution Account, and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions deduct 'amounts required to be reimbursed pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.03' without mentioning this section.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"A single short sentence imposing a plain duty.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b) and the Remittance Date definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence; clear in effect.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b)'s contemplation that the Master Servicer may act as servicer.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"The required coverage is only 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — an undefined market standard with no floor.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes a coverage amount or gives anyone the right to approve the bond, so the standard is left entirely at large in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"Combines an open grant ('any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable, including but not limited to') with four enumerated powers, a classic general-versus-specific tension, and the REMIC proviso turns on what is 'reasonably within its control'.","reasoning_cat2":"The grant is made 'subject to the REMIC Provisions and the provisions of Article XI hereof', but Article XI is Termination, which has nothing to do with master servicing powers — the cross-reference does not fit.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, if heavily qualified by 'to the extent provided in this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement'.","reasoning_cat2":"It defers wholesale to the Servicing Agreements, which are exhibits rather than operative text here; no internal conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and mechanical, with an electronic-signature accommodation; the parenthetical '(or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may)' makes the backstop permissive rather than mandatory.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Request for Release definition and Exhibit G.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"It refers to 'Such trust receipt' although no trust receipt has been mentioned — only a request for release — so the antecedent is missing, and the final clause releases the file on liquidation rather than requiring its return.","reasoning_cat2":"The Request for Release definition and Section 4.07(a) use a certification, not a trust receipt, so the term has no referent elsewhere in the Agreement.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"The access sentence is garbled — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access ... to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — leaving it unclear who is entitled to access.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.01 contains a parallel access provision with a different list of grantees and an express Mortgagor-privacy proviso that this subsection lacks.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.28}
]}

{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as to parties and date.","reasoning_cat2":"The Yield Maintenance Agreement definition already sweeps in any credit support annex, and Section 5.04 bears the same heading, so this term is duplicative.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"Three long parallel allocation paragraphs; mechanical and internally consistent, if hard to read.","reasoning_cat2":"It dovetails with the Current Interest and Uncertificated Accrued Interest definitions, which both point back to this section; the reference to Section 6.02 coverage is outside the supplied text.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"The granting language is garbled in places ('all the right, title and interest of the Sellers in and to the assets in the Mortgage Loans'), and the delivery obligations shift unpredictably between 'the Depositor' and 'the Seller may deliver', with a one-year title-policy grace built into limb (v).","reasoning_cat2":"Its final paragraph says the Special Deposit 'will be transferred by EMC', while the Special Deposit definition says it is 'deposited into the Trust by the Depositor'; and the conveyance of 'the Trust Fund' must be squared with the Trust Fund definition, which omits the Bring Down Agreements that Section 2.02(d) requires the Trustee to enforce.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the ungrammatical 'will deliver to the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee an Initial Certification', and the review standard mixes a duty to 'ascertain' with permission to 'conclusively rely' on execution and genuineness.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to loans 'identified in Exhibit B to this Agreement, as supplemented', while the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition contemplates amendment for substitutions rather than supplementation; the interaction with Section 2.02(c)'s cure/repurchase remedy is also left implicit.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"A definite 180-day review with a stated notification duty; 'appear defective on its face' is a soft but conventional standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Custodian to notify only 'the Sellers', whereas Section 2.02(c) makes both the Sellers and the related Originators potential repurchasers of defective loans.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"The closing sentence makes cure/repurchase/substitution 'the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — a limitation that names two persons but conspicuously omits the Trustee and the Trust, an expressio unius problem on the face of the words.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.02(d) separately empowers the Trustee to enforce repurchase obligations 'on behalf of the Trust', and Section 2.03 provides a separate repurchase mechanic, so the reach of this sole-remedy sentence against those provisions is genuinely contestable.","prob_cat1":0.58,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"The duty extends to repurchase obligations 'and any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation' the Sponsor's Accredited backstop — a general catch-all followed by one specific, raising ejusdem generis and expressio unius questions about the backstop's scope.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be read against Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence and against the Trust Fund definition, which conveys 'the rights under the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement' but does not mention the Bring Down Agreements the Trustee is told to enforce.","prob_cat1":0.55,"prob_cat2":0.53},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"The notice paragraph turns on 'discovery' of a breach that 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders' and requires 'prompt written notice', all elastic terms; the deposit timing is keyed to the Determination Date, of which there are two.","reasoning_cat2":"The section is headed as containing only the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations, yet it houses the substitution and repurchase machinery that the Replacement Mortgage Loan definition, Section 2.05 and Section 4.02 all cross-refer to as if it contained loan-level representations.","prob_cat1":0.49,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence survival clause; on its own terms it is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the Section 2.03 representations survive 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', which makes sense only for loan-level representations, whereas Section 2.03 contains corporate representations of Wells Fargo; the Mortgage Loans definition also cites a non-existent 'Section 2.03(b)(v)' representation.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.46},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"The final paragraph reads 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach', omitting a conjunction, and the good-title representation is given without any stated remedy for its breach.","reasoning_cat2":"The Depositor's good-title representation sits against Section 2.01's conveyance and Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence, which addresses only document defects, leaving unclear what follows from a breach of this representation.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"Opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and turns on whether 'default is not reasonably foreseeable', a forward-looking judgment with no decision-maker specified.","reasoning_cat2":"It overrides the repurchase timing in Sections 2.02 and 2.03, which themselves set fixed Determination Date deposit dates, so the two timing regimes must be reconciled.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"Gives the Seller or Originator an option among cure, substitution and repurchase 'at such party's option', with a 90-day outside date attaching only to limb (iii).","reasoning_cat2":"It requires substitution to satisfy 'the conditions in Section 2.03', but Section 2.03's substitution paragraph bars any substitution after the second anniversary of the Closing Date, which would leave later-discovered non-qualified mortgages with only cure or repurchase.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"A short acknowledgment and declaration of trust; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and the Trustee definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC II recital and the Class R-2 Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC III recital and the Class R-3 Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC IV recital and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC V recital and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"Standard conveyance language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the REMIC VI recital, Section 4.22(a) and the Class RX Certificate definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"Limbs (d) and (e) are open-ended catch-alls ('necessary, suitable or convenient ... or are incidental thereto or connected therewith') sitting against three specific purposes, and the final sentence trails off with the dangling 'and this Section 2.07'.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (b) says the Trust issues 'the Certificates sold to the Depositor in exchange for the Mortgage Loans', while Section 2.01 and the Preliminary Statement describe the exchange as being for the whole Trust Fund.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"Grants 'full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable' and then imposes a series of specific monitoring duties, so the interaction of the open grant with the specific duties is contestable.","reasoning_cat2":"The open grant sits against the objective Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard in the same section and against Section 4.05's identically worded grant, which is expressly made subject to the REMIC Provisions.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Three specific prohibitions with defined exceptions; reasonably tight, though 'comply with any directions of the Seller, the Servicers or the Master Servicer' is an unqualified obedience duty.","reasoning_cat2":"It excepts substitutions 'pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or Section 2.03 of this Agreement', consistently with Section 2.03's substitution paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"Turns on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment' and on what it 'deems appropriate', and permits reliance on an Officer's Certificate without further inquiry.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out for Wells Fargo as Servicer aligns with Section 4.03(b)-(c), which route Wells Fargo terminations through the Trustee instead.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"The enforcement standard — such extent and time as the Master Servicer 'in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans' — is an elastic hypothetical-owner test, and the last sentence's 'Successor master Servicer' is inconsistently capitalised.","reasoning_cat2":"The final sentence conditions the Trustee's assumption of duties on the Trustee 'not been able to find a successor servicer or a Successor master Servicer', which sits awkwardly with the mandatory termination duties earlier in the same subsection and with Section 8.07.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"Two long parallel reimbursement regimes, each with an 'including, without limitation' list; the trigger 'not fully and timely reimbursed' has no stated deadline.","reasoning_cat2":"Reimbursement comes from the Distribution Account, and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds definitions deduct 'amounts required to be reimbursed pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.03' without mentioning this section.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"A single short sentence imposing a plain duty.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b) and the Remittance Date definition.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence; clear in effect.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b)'s contemplation that the Master Servicer may act as servicer.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"The required coverage is only 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — an undefined market standard with no floor.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes a coverage amount or gives anyone the right to approve the bond, so the standard is left entirely at large in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"Combines an open grant ('any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable, including but not limited to') with four enumerated powers, a classic general-versus-specific tension, and the REMIC proviso turns on what is 'reasonably within its control'.","reasoning_cat2":"The grant is made 'subject to the REMIC Provisions and the provisions of Article XI hereof', but Article XI is Termination, which has nothing to do with master servicing powers — the cross-reference does not fit.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"Definite, if heavily qualified by 'to the extent provided in this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement'.","reasoning_cat2":"It defers wholesale to the Servicing Agreements, which are exhibits rather than operative text here; no internal conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and mechanical, with an electronic-signature accommodation; the parenthetical '(or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may)' makes the backstop permissive rather than mandatory.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Request for Release definition and Exhibit G.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"It refers to 'Such trust receipt' although no trust receipt has been mentioned — only a request for release — so the antecedent is missing, and the final clause releases the file on liquidation rather than requiring its return.","reasoning_cat2":"The Request for Release definition and Section 4.07(a) use a certification, not a trust receipt, so the term has no referent elsewhere in the Agreement.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"The access sentence is garbled — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access ... to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — leaving it unclear who is entitled to access.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.01 contains a parallel access provision with a different list of grantees and an express Mortgagor-privacy proviso that this subsection lacks.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.28}
]}
